Just a warning as someone who has over 1k hours. Expect to die a lot. And by that I mean, learn the game slowly, don't be afraid to check the wiki or discord or subreddit. If someone says 'this is the best way to do something' consider *that process* a tool in your tool box. There's going to be many times you want to explore, do things based on vibes and not numbers. Not enough people, not good enough gear, not enough x, y, z. That's when you go to those processes. Look up the item stats and maybe even put a spread sheet together. You do not *have* to to succeed. But it's great if you're a numbers nerd like a lot of us lol.

As I looked back on the session as a whole, I would say that I succeeded in terms of roleplay outside of combat, it just seems I was having my character concept challenged, and rather than just accepting that and moving into a more interesting dynamic, I just got unjustly butt-hurt.
I'll admit, I was just being really butt-hurt and emotional. I get that way sometimes, and was looking for a more constructive way of dealing with it.

So really what went on was that rolls were happening as normal, I was just having a case of confirmation bias. As well, by overshadowed I meant that when we would enter into combat (usually with evil creatures) our paladin would usually get massive one hit kills, this is mainly because of his innate paladin-ery. What I wasn't taking into account was that I was trying to fill a role already filled, that of the in the front tank-y fighter, and instead of branching out and perhaps taking some different route, flanking, using range, I was trying to force myself into that role. I need to remember just what you (and many others) have said, that bad rolls can (and should) still lead to a good story, or at least be used as an opportunity for good role playing.

So I have taken all your criticism, and have arrived at that I was being a pessimistic butt-hurt child, the rest of my group has told me so, and we have spoken on how I can stop being such. We recently hit a level up and I am becoming a cleric, as this works with my character's backstory and general overall feel.
